COMPARISON:  comparison is made to a prior outside mammogram of January 21, 2015.  FINDINGS: A bilateral mammogram dated January 22, 2016 is submitted for review. The  breasts are heterogeneously dense with nodularity, unchanged from the  prior outside mammogram of 2015. No suspicious lesion is seen  mammographically.  The patient then underwent bilateral pre-and postcontrast breast MRI on  June 23, 2016. In the left breast a focal area of enhancement was seen  measuring 3 x 3 x 5 mm (series 12, image 55) for which biopsy was  recommended.of note, the small area of enhancement closely abuts a cyst.  Static images from a left breast ultrasound on July 6, 2016 demonstrate a  cyst at the 2:00 site 5 cm from the nipple in the left breast. There is a  small irregular area labeled at the 2:00 site 4 cm from the nipple in the  left breast which is unmeasured but appears less than 1 cm in size. By  report, no definite correlate was seen for the area of MR enhancement.  The patient underwent MR guided biopsy on August 2, 2016 of the left area  of enhancement yielding ALH with columnar cell changes without evidence of  invasive malignancy. the needle appears to transverse the breasts lateral  to medial possibly to a site slightly deeper than the prior images of June  23 suggesting a more central area of enhancement. the area of enhancement  nor the clip are clearly seen on the images at the time of biopsy.A clip  was placed by report.  A unilateral left postbiopsy mammogram was performed on August 2, 2016  showing postbiopsy changes in the medial breast with a clip slightly more  lateral to the area of postbiopsy change.  Multiple images from a left needle localization for excisional biopsy  dated September 6, 2016 are submitted for review. The approach was in the  straight lateral projection from the lateral skin surface. The wire  appears to have been placed at an adequate location following some  repositioning. No specimen radiograph was submitted however on the report  of the specimen radiograph the wire is included but no clip was seen.  A unilateral left mammogram dated September 28, 2006 shows the clip  remains in the left breast.  The results of the excisional biopsy are certainly concordant with the MR  guided biopsy in that they both yielded ALH with columnar cell changes.  The excisional biopsy did show postbiopsy changes presumably from the MR  guided biopsy. Therefore, even though the clip was not removed, the  excision most likely did include the sampling site from MR biopsy.  Consideration could be given to repeating the MR approximately 6 months  after the biopsy to again assess the area of enhancement due to the  discrepancy with the clip.

Initial injection of 7 mL of MultiHance infiltrated into the patient's  right antecubital fossa. The patient was assessed in the MRI suite. There  was mild swelling of the antecubital fossa. The patient reported localized  pain in the region. No reported numbness, tingling, or strength deficits.   As the patient requested proceeded with the study, a new IV was placed by  the radiology nursing staff.  The patient was instructed to seek emergency care should the pain  increased or if there was a development of numbness, tingling, weakness,  or perfusion deficits to the distal right upper extremity. Patient was  counseled to keep the arm elevated and that warm and/or cold compresses  could be applied to the area for symptomatic relief. The patient indicated  understanding of these instructions.  The study proceeded without incident and the patient was discharged from  the radiology department in stable condition. On the right home, the  patient called back to the radiology department and reported possible  swelling and tingling of the lips. The patient denied any difficulty  breathing. The patient was counseled that since we were unable to direct  examine her, if there was any concern for an allergic reaction, she should  proceed to the emergency department for additional evaluation/treatment. Pre-gadolinium, arterial, and interstitial phases of enhancement were  obtained sequentially. Delayed axial T1 weighted images were obtained.  Subtraction images were generated by post processing. FINDINGS: Bilateral breasts: Skin resolution is limited due to motion artifact. There are scattered  fibroglandular densities. There is moderate background parenchymal  enhancement.  Right breast: There is architectural distortion in the upper outer quadrant associated  with biopsy clip, the appearance in keeping with biopsy proven invasive  lobular carcinoma. The extent of disease is difficult to measure due to  the infiltrative appearance of the mass and adjacent moderate background  enhancement. The dominant mass in the upper outer quadrant measures  approximately 40 x 30 x 22 mm. However the enhancing architectural  distortion extends anteriorly towards the nipple over a distance of  approximately 40 mm, suspicious for extension towards the nipple. This is  best appreciated on series 7 image 42. There are additional scattered  enhancing foci elsewhere in the breast which are nonspecific in  appearance. No suspicious adenopathy is seen.  Left breast: There is a biopsy clip. There are multiple scattered enhancing foci  throughout the breast which are nonspecific. No dominant enhancement  suspicious for malignancy is seen. No suspicious adenopathy seen.

The entire process spans 3.3  cm in transverse dimension and 3 cm in AP dimension (series 6:  Image 54).   This is immediately inferior to the recent malignant biopsy marker. It is unclear if this is enhancing  postsurgical scar versus residual/recurrent disease.

FINDINGS: The breast has scattered fibroglandular tissue. The background parenchymal enhancement is moderate and multi-nodular.  There are 2 core biopsy clips in the superior central right breast,  marking areas of known malignancy:   -The 1st is seen on series 6, image 65, associated with a hematoma and  clumped nodular enhancement which measures at least 3 cm in greatest  dimension, from anterior to posterior (series 6, image 62).  Enhancement  extending to the skin laterally is seen nearby, most consistent with  biopsy change (series 6, image 67). -The 2nd core biopsy clip is more superior and seen on series 6, image 82,  associated with clumped masslike nodular enhancement measuring about 2.2  cm in greatest dimension, from inferior to superior (series 101, image  46). The 2 sites of known malignancy are about 1.5 cm apart from superior to  inferior (series 101, image 45) on this modality, and if overall measured  together abnormal enhancement spans about 5.5 cm from superior to inferior  (also seen on series 101, image 45).  There are 2 subcentimeter masses in close proximity to the to index  malignancies: -1 of these measures 7 mm, and is less than 1.5 cm inferior and posterior  to the more inferior location of known malignancy (series 101, image 50). -The 2nd of these measures 3 mm and is less than 1.5 cm lateral to the  approximate midway point between the 2 sites of known malignancy (series  6, image 72). These 2 subcentimeter masses are concerning given their proximity to the  patient's known malignancy, although other scattered foci of enhancement  which are most in keeping with background parenchymal enhancement appear  similar, particularly in comparison to the 3 mm finding laterally.  No unique suspicious enhancement in the left breast.  No suspicious lymph  nodes seen.
